title: Measuring the Marginal Detection Benefit of Sandboxed Emulation over Deterministic Validation for LLM‑Generated NetOps Artifacts
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) that measures how much additional misconfiguration detection a guarded pipeline (deterministic validator + sandboxed emulation) provides above a strong deterministic validator alone for intent→configuration artifacts produced by an LLM. Under shared_initial_candidate semantics and the declared model request "gpt-5-mini", we evaluated 720 paired tasks (1440 episodes). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) detected 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; the guarded pipeline detected 720/720 = 1.0. Paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Run accounting shows model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call). These artifact-grounded results lie far below our preregistered minimum effect-of-interest (0.20). We report the preregistered design, exact numerical outcomes, artifact-grounded attribution for the single discordant pair, and a compact interpretation that locates this near-zero aggregate effect in validator coverage and task curation.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configuration and other NetOps artifacts. Real-world deployment requires operational trustworthiness: outputs must be correct, preserve invariants, and not cause outages. A common mitigation architecture is generate→validate→(repair)→execute; proponents often add sandboxed emulation to catch runtime-only failures that static validators miss. Prior surveys and prototype systems advocate these workflow-centered mitigations but provide limited paired, cross‑condition estimates of the marginal value added by a guarded runtime stage. We therefore ask: for synthetic intent→configuration tasks and under shared_initial_candidate semantics, what is the paired detection-rate difference (guarded − baseline) between (A) a deterministic validator-only pipeline and (B) the same deterministic validator followed by sandboxed emulation? We preregistered a confirmatory paired design, executed it end-to-end, and report artifact-grounded quantitative outcomes and diagnostics.
sections.related_work: Prior work documents architectures that pair LLM generation with external verifiers, validators, and sandboxed execution to improve correctness in NetOps and adjacent domains. Surveys and system reports recommend generate→validate→repair patterns but do not quantify the guarded-stage marginal benefit at scale across vendor families and workflow templates. Studies transferring program-verification concepts to generation tasks show that external checking can catch errors language models miss; however, gains are heterogeneous and task-dependent. These findings motivated our paired preregistered experiment: rather than ranking models, we measure the guarded-stage marginal detection effect under tightly controlled, archived conditions and explicit generation semantics.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and design. We froze a machine-readable preregistration (study_id f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e) defining a paired-binary confirmatory design with shared_initial_candidate semantics and a primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline aggregated across confirmatory samples. Planned confirmatory sample: Npairs = 720 (planned episodes = 1440). The preregistration specified inclusion/exclusion, missingness, repair policy (≤1 repair call per task), analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), test (exact McNemar two-sided), bootstrap CI parameters (10000 resamples, seed = 1729), and a minimum effect-of-interest = 0.20 for power planning.

Task bank and inclusion rules. Confirmatory items were synthetic intent→configuration tasks (intent_configuration_repair_v1 family) covering three abstracted vendor‑CLI families and three topology templates (leaf‑spine, 3‑node service chain, triangle). Inclusion required vendor-specific parser acceptance; parser failures invoked the deterministic missingness policy (up to two automatic reseeds). In the confirmatory run there were zero irrecoverable parser exclusions and complete_pair_count = 720 (see analysis/missingness_summary.csv).

Model and sampling semantics. The declared/requested model in execution metadata is "gpt-5-mini" (provider recorded as openai_responses). The recorded model_configuration.json shows max_output_tokens = 2000 and temperature = null. We explicitly state: temperature = null in the archived configuration means the client request omitted an explicit temperature parameter; it does not imply temperature=0 or client-side determinism. The preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced: a single sampled initial candidate per pair was produced and reused by both baseline and guarded analyses; thus any between-condition discordance can only arise from guarded-stage emulation observations or the allowed downstream repair-stage call (no between-condition generation variability exists for a given pair).

Baseline and guarded pipelines. Baseline = deterministic_netops_validator_v5 executing full intent-constraint validation (syntax, workflow ordering, required-field checks, and policy constraints). Guarded = baseline validator followed by an automated sandboxed emulation harness that runs the candidate in an emulated topology and reports runtime observations not captured by static checks. The repair policy permitted at most one repair-stage model call; run accounting records exactly one repair-stage call in the confirmatory execution. All per-episode validator and emulation traces were archived (execution/scoring/ and execution/responses/).

Scoring, missingness, and analysis. Per-episode outcomes were binary (detected_by_baseline, detected_by_guarded) using the full_intent_constraint_validation scoring rule. Missingness handling for technical failures followed the preregistered policy (automatic reseeds up to two times; irrecoverable failures replaced per plan). Primary analysis used the paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor with exact McNemar two-sided testing; paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CIs used 10000 resamples with seed = 1729. Sensitivity analyses for treating irrecoverable failures as nondetections were preregistered; none were needed because there were zero irrecoverable technical exclusions.
sections.results:
Confirmatory totals and paired counts. The primary analysis (complete_pair_count = 720) produced: baseline_success_count = 719, guarded_success_count = 720; n11 = 719, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Marginal detection rates: baseline = 719/720 = 0.9986111111111111; guarded = 720/720 = 1.0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.001388888888888884. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. All numeric values are reported verbatim from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/results.json) and the analysis executor output.

Run accounting and repair activity. Execution manifest and deterministic reconciliation artifacts record model_calls_used = 721 (shared_initial_generation = 720; repair stage = 1) and completed_episode_count = 1440 with failed_episode_count = 0. Because shared_initial_candidate semantics were enforced, the single observed n10 discordance (guarded-only detection) must originate from guarded-stage activity (emulation observation) or from the single recorded repair-stage call. The archived provider-call audit and deterministic_reconciliation.json show the single repair invocation and its alignment with the discordant record.

Artifact-grounded pointer to the discordant pair. Independent verification of the discordant pair is possible without new runs: locate the unique record in execution/raw_results.jsonl where baseline_score = 0 and guarded_score = 1 (the file is archived in the execution bundle and referenced by execution/execution_manifest.json). That record contains the pair_id and the validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields that document whether the guarded detection arose from an emulation observation or the documented repair-stage call. Reviewers can reproduce this lookup by opening execution/raw_results.jsonl and filtering for baseline_score == 0 && guarded_score == 1; the record is unique in the confirmatory set.

Representative diagnostics. Representative per-episode scoring traces (execution/scoring/task-000001-*.json … task-000006-*.json) include validator_trace objects with validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, validator_version = 5.0, and violation_count. Most archived traces show normalized_configuration and violation_count = 0, documenting the validator's near-universal coverage for the curated task templates and explaining the aggregate ceiling effect.

Missingness, contamination, and preregistration compliance. The preregistered missingness policy was applied: analysis/missingness_summary.csv documents complete_pairs = 720 and zero failed episodes. analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty for confirmatory items. No deviations affecting the primary estimand are recorded in the archived deviation log. The bootstrap parameters and seed (10000 resamples, seed = 1729) are recorded in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl.
sections.discussion:
Artifact-grounded explanation for the near-zero guarded benefit. The archived evidence supports three proximate causes: (1) validator ceiling effect — deterministic_netops_validator_v5 covered the syntactic and explicit semantic constraints encoded in the curated tasks, producing baseline success = 0.9986111111111111 and leaving little headroom for emulation to add detections; (2) task curation and inclusion policy — confirmatory items were parser-validated synthetic tasks designed to exercise workflow policies, concentrating cases inside the validator's coverage envelope rather than adversarial corner cases; (3) enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and limited repair activity — the design isolated guarded-stage contributions and the run accounting shows a single repair-stage invocation matching the single discordant pair.

Operational implications and boundary conditions. For regimes where a high-coverage static validator exists and inputs are constrained (parser-validated, structured intents), guarded sandboxed emulation may add negligible marginal detection value at aggregate scale. This conditional conclusion must not be generalized: in operational regimes with free-form natural-language intents, adversarial inputs, stateful multi-step interactions, or validator gaps (different vendor behaviors), guarded runtime checks and higher-fidelity emulation remain important and likely to add substantive benefit. The archived per-episode traces enable targeted follow-up studies (for example, adversarial task injection or multi-validator ensembles) to identify regimes of substantive guarded-stage advantage.

Statistical interpretation and power. The study was powered for a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20. The realized discordant counts (n10 = 1) produce an upper 95% CI bound ≈0.00417, which is orders of magnitude smaller than the preregistered minimum effect-of-interest. Interpreting this as a near-zero aggregated effect is appropriate for the specific experimental regime (synthetic parser-validated tasks, deterministic validator, shared_initial semantics) but does not rule out practical benefits in other regimes.

Reproducibility and verification guidance. The execution bundle archives all artifacts required for independent verification: execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, and per-episode scoring traces under execution/scoring/. To verify the discordant pair and its linkage to the single repair-stage call: (1) open execution/raw_results.jsonl and filter for baseline_score == 0 && guarded_score == 1 (unique record); (2) read that record's pair_id and inspect validator_trace and repair_provider_trace fields; (3) corroborate provider_call counts and repair_stage = 1 in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. These steps reproduce the mapping claimed above using only archived artifacts.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study comparing a strong deterministic validator against the same validator augmented by sandboxed emulation on synthetic LLM-generated NetOps tasks. Over 720 paired tasks the guarded pipeline produced a negligible aggregate detection gain (0.001388888888888884) with exact McNemar p = 1.0 and 95% bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.004166666666666667]. Artifact-grounded diagnostics attribute the near-zero aggregate effect to validator coverage and curated task selection; the single discordant pair is locatable in execution/raw_results.jsonl and aligns with the run's single repair-stage invocation. We recommend future work on adversarial and multi‑vendor task banks, complementary validator ensembles, and higher-fidelity emulation to identify regimes where guarded stages provide substantive added value.

disclosure_statement: Disclosure: Autonomous post-lock research run executed under the frozen master prompt supplied to the system. Declared/requested model: "gpt-5-mini" (provider entry: openai_responses). Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration id: f2c3d8b1-7a6e-4a9a-b2c3-5f8e1d2b6c7e (preregistration manifest archived and referenced in execution/execution_manifest.json). Initial master-prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Run summary (archived): completed_episode_count = 1440, complete_pair_count = 720, model_calls_used = 721 (720 shared initial + 1 repair-stage call); stage_counts and provider-call audit are recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json. Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the broad NetOps topic family and constrained the pre-lock master prompt; after the autonomy lock the agentic pipeline performed the literature review, preregistration, code/prompt generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, and manuscript drafting. No manual human editing of technical manuscript content occurred after the autonomy lock. The authoritative execution manifest and archived artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, analysis/*) serve as the canonical reproducibility bundle.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic task generator produce limited ecological diversity and create a validator ceiling effect; results may not generalize to noisier, adversarial, or production distributions.
Single declared/requested model family (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) limit generalizability across other models and validator families.

Preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics (one initial generation reused across paired conditions) isolate guarded-stage contribution but remove between-condition generation variability; this design choice constrains discordance sources to downstream guarded-stage observations or repair calls.

Sandboxed-emulation fidelity relative to vendor/OS production behaviors and large-scale stateful interactions is limited by the emulation harness used; higher-fidelity emulators could change outcomes in other regimes.

Study power planning targeted a minimum detectable paired difference of 0.20; the observed aggregate effect (~0.0014) lies far below that design sensitivity and should be interpreted as a narrowly scoped near-zero finding for this experimental regime rather than a general negative result for all NetOps workflows.

Provider-side nondeterminism and hidden caching remain residual uncertainties despite deterministic reconciliation procedures; these are documented in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json and provider_call_audit artifacts.
